persons.note: After 14 August: Wounded in the right foot; taken down the Illinois River, ransomed by Thomas Forsyth (two mares and a keg), reached St Louis 14 Oct 1812; rejoined his wife at his father's in New York, March 1813.

persons.name: Margaret Helm

born.note: The date as the cited source prints it.

present_on_scene_date.note: Helm's narrative and Wau-Bun (her own account) put her on horseback in the march and battle. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Eleanor Kinzie's daughter by her first marriage (to McKillip), married to Lieutenant Helm. Wau-Bun's massacre narrative is "represented as being quoted directly from her" (Quaife App. II), told ~20 years later; Quaife doubts its details. No children. After 14 August: Saved (Wau-Bun: by Black Partridge); taken across to the Kinzie house; with the Kinzies to St Joseph and Detroit; reached Helm's father's home in New York a week before her husband, March 1813.
